$comment: Ratcheted quality budgets (issue 578). Enforced by `npm run verify:budgets`.
1. CI fails when a measured value EXCEEDS its budget. Existing debt never blocks
work; only adding to it does.
2. CI also fails on UNCLAIMED SLACK - a value measurably better than its budget
without the budget being lowered. Without this the ratchet stops ratcheting and
the gate silently degrades into a no-op.
3. Every change to a value REQUIRES `finding` and `justifiedBy` to be updated.
A budget moved without a cited finding and commit is not reviewable.
Every initial value was transcribed from a committed artifact under audit/, never
typed from memory. The first transcription attempt read contaminated artifacts left
behind by the mutation harness and produced 74/16/88/1703; the harness now restores
clean artifacts and asserts no mutant marker survives. These are the clean figures.

themeMatrixUntraceableRate.justifiedBy: issue 625, two defects fixed together, both in this gate's own machinery rather than in the rendered page. (1) The oracle: this sweep tracks color/background-color/border-color/border-radius/padding/font-size/font-weight/box-shadow/transition-duration/outline-width, but only ever probed a token's resolved value through FOUR CSS properties: color, padding-top, border-top-width, font-size. A token whose only expression is a font-weight, a box-shadow or a transition-duration shares no value space with any of those four, so it could never appear in the oracle - every element rendering it, even correctly from a real token, was misclassified untraceable. Brought to parity with the shared render classifier's probe set (render-capture.mjs), which already covered these categories. (2) Mantine's ScrollArea ships its own static scrollbar padding/transition in ScrollArea.css ('padding: calc(--scrollarea-scrollbar-size / 5)', a 150ms transition), untouched by any GDS theme override; both classifiers now exempt it by selector (mantine-ScrollArea-scrollbar/-thumb) rather than inventing a token for browser-chrome geometry that was never a design decision. Measured rate fell 26.83 -> 15.67 (26368 properties, 4133 untraceable) on the same 52-cell sweep, same commit, same tree - not a design fix, two broken rulers replaced. Two more fixed in the same investigation, both real: Chrome serializes a resolved color-mix() as color(srgb r g b / a), never rgb() - the same fix already shipped once for the identical reason in verify-badge-contrast-runtime.mjs. And Mantine's own border-top-width: calc(0.0625rem * var(--mantine-scale)) formula is now resolved and indexed directly, rather than left permanently untraceable because it combines a literal with a variable instead of referencing one custom property (both classifiers recognize the same resolvable Mantine constant; a border-top-style must be set on the probe first, or the UA reports 0 regardless of the declared width - the same lesson as the outline-width fix, applied to a second property). Final: 15.4% (26368 properties, 4061 untraceable), same 52-cell sweep.
themeMatrixUntraceableRate.$comment: The old headroom is gone. This sat at 34 to clear an observed 33.94-33.96 band with element counts varying by ~114 between runs, which meant a genuine 0.05pp regression was indistinguishable from noise. The band was render timing, not measurement error. The artifact now records exact counts rather than bucketing them to the nearest thousand, because reproducibility is what makes that precision honest. KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than implied: 36 of the cells hit the 400-element sample cap, so those routes are sampled rather than swept exhaustively - the true rate could differ on the unsampled remainder. cellsTruncatedAtSampleCap in the artifact reports it every run.

untraceableRenderRate.justifiedBy: issue 627: this rate had drifted from its 7.2% baseline without the classifier changing - a fresh Phase 1 re-run on the SAME 40 cells measured 9.857% (28962/293814), observation count up ~53% and literal count up ~110% since the baseline, meaning new content since the last correction is disproportionately untokenized. Investigated rather than silently ratcheted: closed four real, verified gaps in this pass. (1) render-capture.mjs itself had the theme-matrix oracle's exact gap class - TRACKED checked font-size and all four border-radius corners and both gap axes with no matching probe; fixed. (2) The color-mix()/color(srgb...) serialization gap (see themeMatrixUntraceableRate). (3) A naive value.split(',') shredded any multi-value transition-timing-function containing 2+ comma-separated cubic-bezier() functions mid-parenthesis ('cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1), cubic-bezier(...)' became eight unmatchable fragments) - the single largest fix this pass; replaced with a paren-depth-aware split. (4) Mantine's border-top-width hairline formula, recognized directly (see themeMatrixUntraceableRate). Two real, GDS-owned literals also fixed at the source, not the classifier: .gds-tour-launch/.gds-tour-btn/.gds-tour-card__actions (packages/gds-theme/styles.css) now reference --gds-space-*/--gds-font-size-* tokens instead of bare rem values, and PublicShell's headerVariant='compact' now references --gds-space-3xl (the only one of its three header heights that lands exactly on an existing step). Result: 9.857% -> 7.428%, closing 91% of the regression. The remainder is understood, not unexplained: PublicShell's other two header heights (72px, 88px) don't land close enough to any existing space step to swap in without a visible resize - a new token value, not a rounding, left as a recorded decision pending an owner call; several Mantine components (SegmentedControl, Button-inner) declare component-scoped custom properties or plain literal transitions this methodology cannot see from a document-body probe, the same limitation already diagnosed for Badge's font-size; and .gds-tour-card__progress's letter-spacing has no GDS tracking/letter-spacing token axis to reference at all. Render mutants M1/M2 remain the validity proof of the instrument.

tokensWithGaps.justifiedBy: issue 618: back to 78. --gds-vibe-swatch was documented rather than left as debt -- THEME_GOVERNANCE.md explains the two atmosphere scales and when to use each, styles.css declares a default and a [data-gds-theme-swatch] surface that references it, and the tokens page lists it. All five obligations (listed/demoed/explained/variationsShown/useCase) are met, so the new token cost nothing.
tokensWithGaps.$comment: Issue 612 RESOLVED for the drift half: forward-trace.mjs and dimensions.mjs now run inside artifacts:refresh, so this artifact is regenerated every cycle instead of only when someone remembered to run audit:refresh. The caveat this comment used to carry - that the true gap was this figure OR MORE - no longer applies. Proof the drift was real: the committed dimensions.json recorded 1293 site phrase keys while the packs held 1297. 612 CLOSED: the 9 gaps (focus-ring x4, density, identity-unresolved, motion-duration-ambient, transition-scope, text-on-support) are classified in scripts/audit/forward-trace.config.mjs with verified reasons and review dates (2026-11-01). Classified means explained, not excused - they still count here, and this ratchet only moves down by actually closing one.

unreachableTokens.justifiedBy: issue 586: all 15 F13 tokens classified — 14 extension points with reasons and expiry dates, 1 pending wire-up tracked as issue 591. 0 remain unclassified.
unreachableTokens.$comment: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE ZERO. 0 does NOT mean 'no unreachable tokens exist' — 15 tokens are still referenced by nothing. It means 0 are UNCLASSIFIED. The gate's job is that no token can be declared without a written, dated disposition; it is not that every token renders. The classification counts (extensionPoints, pendingWireUp) are in the same artifact and are the numbers to read for remediation progress. Measurement also changed source here: the old value came from forward-trace.json#/rows[!demoed] (Phase 2 demo reachability, a different question) and is now the reachability census. Stated per the F24 rule.

publishedGraphOverlap.justifiedBy: issue 595: badge tone pairs add 20 roles. Issue 593: the accent axis adds 50 roles. Issue 558: the reaction axis adds 14 roles. Issue 557: the typography and elevation axes add 34 roles. Issue 556: the density axis adds 16 --gds-space-*/--gds-control-height-*/--gds-density roles. Issue 555: the shape axis adds 21 --gds-radius-* roles (7 steps + 14 semantic roles) to the 34 from issue 585. All 55 runtime semantic roles are published per theme per scheme; coverage 55/55 = 100%.
publishedGraphOverlap.$comment: Was 1 — the published graph and the runtime semantic set overlapped only on `accent`, so a design tool importing the graph received 17 atmosphere colours and none of the roles that determine what a component looks like. Direction is `min`, so this can only go up: dropping a semantic role from the published graph now fails the release.

undeclaredMantineDependencies.justifiedBy: issue 589 census: 92 consumed, 4 governed by gdsTheme, 6 delegated with reasons, 1 dynamic, 8 lane-only, 73 ungoverned. Budget = 73 ungoverned + 8 lane-only. Ratcheted 81 -> 80 (issue 597): LabelTag stopped rendering a raw Mantine palette colour as text, removing one ungoverned consumption. Claimed rather than banked — the slack left the mantine-governance mutant alive, since adding a variable back landed inside the unclaimed headroom and the gate stayed green.
undeclaredMantineDependencies.$comment: MEASUREMENT CHANGED in issue 589, stated rather than slipped in (the F24 lesson). The old value 87 came from dimensions.json#/themeControl/mantineVarsGdsConsumesButNeverDeclares and meant 'consumed but never DECLARED as a CSS custom property'. The new value means 'consumed but not DICTATED by the default gdsTheme', measured by comparing gdsTheme against Mantine's DEFAULT_THEME, with reasoned delegations excluded. 87 -> 81 is NOT 6 variables remediated: nothing was declared and no rendered value changed. The two counts answer different questions, and only the new one distinguishes a value GDS actually controls from one it merely writes down.

registryAtomsWithoutCoverage.justifiedBy: issue 581 - every registry kind is now either obligation-modelled or explicitly covered elsewhere with a named gate/phase. NOTE: the MEASUREMENT CHANGED. It previously counted atoms in kinds with no audit-phase coverage (1699); it now counts atoms in kinds with neither an obligation model nor a recorded owner (0). The 1699 did not vanish - 410 of those atoms have real unmet obligations and are tracked by the separate obligationGaps budget below.

localesWithoutSitePack.justifiedBy: issue 587: ja, ko and zh site phrase packs generated through the existing generator, so every package locale now has a site pack. Parity is enforced BETWEEN the corpora by verify:locale-coverage — the gap existed because coverage was only ever verified within each corpus separately.

englishLeakageWorstLocale.justifiedBy: issue 611: the seven Hebrew phrases the endpoint could not translate now carry owner-approved translations, so he dropped to 0 and the worst site locale is de at 0.15% (three English loanword phrases German renders verbatim, budgeted in i18n-leakage.config.mjs).
englishLeakageWorstLocale.$comment: MEASUREMENT CHANGED, stated per the F24 rule. The old 3.8% counted every value byte-identical to its English source. That put ~46 non-defects per pack into the number: emails, `Cmd+1`, `npm run verify:references`, component-name lists, and in the package corpus genuine cognates - `Pause`, `Filter` and `Message` are real German and French words. Of 15 package values it flagged, ONE was a real defect. The metric now requires peer evidence that the phrase is translatable (another locale rendered it differently, compared on letters only so an Arabic comma is not mistaken for a translation) plus a script-aware test: any English left in a non-Latin pack is a miss, while a Latin pack is only flagged for prose. The two numbers answer different questions and must never be compared. Remaining: 7 in site/he that machine translation cannot resolve (issue 611) and 2 German loanword phrases, both recorded with reasons in scripts/i18n-leakage.config.mjs.

phase5MutationScore.justifiedBy: Issue 601: renamed from `gateMutationScore`, which read like the GATE SUITE's score and pointed at the Phase 5 render mutants. One word, three referents — the trap F24 named. audit Phase 5 - 6/7 killed, M3 survives, 5 not run, commit bed78c8

renderMutationScore.justifiedBy: issue 579 - M1 and M2 both killed; Phase 1 is only trustworthy while these stay killed

gateSuiteMutationScore.justifiedBy: The gate suite that verifies every OTHER gate was the one gate whose coverage could silently shrink: only `gateSuiteUnexplainedSurvivors` was ratcheted, and deleting a mutant does not raise it — a deleted mutant survives nothing, so the count stays 0 while coverage drops. Seeded at the measured 100% (29 of 29 killed) on 2026-08-13.

gateSuiteUnexplainedSurvivors.justifiedBy: issue 580 - every survivor must be either killed or filed with a dated issue

obligationGaps.justifiedBy: issue 581 - 373 prop jsdoc gaps + 37 variant demo gaps, measured
